title: The Language of the old quarter
premise: Rosalind Quintana, a court translator whose childhood language is dissolving word by word, hears an unrecorded song on the radio — one written decades ago by her father's friend, who died before it could ever be played. The song's survival means someone kept it, and someone betrayed the promise that sealed it. Returning to the Old Quarter, slated for demolition in six weeks, Rosalind must piece together what her family did to protect a murderer or condemn an innocent man, choosing between loyalty to the dead and truth for the living. In the end, she testifies — not in any courtroom, but at the quarter's last public assembly — trading her father's name for the record no one else will keep.
about_author: Felix Blackwood is the pen name of a former interpreter who spent fifteen years in immigration courts before turning to fiction. They write about the words that fall out of languages and the people who catch them.

chapters.title: Borrowed Words
chapters.summary: Rosalind, translating in a drab courtroom, misplaces a word in their mother tongue for the first time in front of a judge. That night, keeping their inventory of unsaid things, they hear a song on the late-radio program: unmistakably their father's friend Mateo's melody, never recorded, never performed after his death. POV Rosalind. Beat: quiet dread cracking open into obsession.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Rosalind rereads their lifelong ledger of withheld statements and finds the entry from age nine: the night Mateo drowned, and what their father made them swear not to say. They call the radio station; the DJ refuses to name the person who submitted the tape. POV Rosalind. Beat: guilt resurfacing as resolve.

chapters.title: Return Ticket
chapters.summary: Rosalind travels back to the Old Quarter, half-shuttered behind demolition notices, and finds their aunt Odalys still running the corner shop. Odalys recognizes the song instantly and goes pale, warning Rosalind that some debts were paid already. POV Rosalind. Beat: homecoming laced with hostility.

chapters.title: What the Walls Kept
chapters.summary: Searching the condemned family house, Rosalind discovers their father's hidden reel-to-reel recordings of Mateo rehearsing — including the song, dated three days before his death. A neighbor, Tomás, watches them enter and leaves without a word. POV Rosalind. Beat: discovery sharpening into suspicion of everyone they loved.

chapters.title: Odalys's Version
chapters.summary: Confronted, Odalys tells her story: Mateo was going to expose the landlord's arson scheme, and Rosalind's father begged him to stay silent for the quarter's survival. She insists he drowned accidentally. Her certainty has a hairline crack in it. POV alternating between Rosalind and Odalys's recounted past. Beat: sympathy complicated by evasion.

chapters.title: Tomás, Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Tomás, the sole holdout refusing relocation, reveals he was with Mateo that night on the pier — and that Rosalind's father arrived after the shouting started. He has waited thirty years for someone to ask. POV Tomás. Beat: the first honest witness, and the first real accusation.

chapters.title: The Second Tape
chapters.summary: The radio DJ, tracked down, admits the tape came from Rosalind's father before his own death — mailed with instructions to play it 'when the buildings come down.' Rosalind realizes their father spent his last years curating a confession he couldn't speak aloud. POV Rosalind. Beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Demolition Eve
chapters.summary: With bulldozers scheduled for morning, Rosalind reconstructs the full night: Mateo fell during a struggle with the landlord's enforcer, and their father helped cover it up to shield the community from retaliation — burying one truth to save a hundred families. POV Rosalind. Beat: the moral weight settling fully onto them.

chapters.title: The Last Assembly
chapters.summary: At the quarter's final town meeting, held in the condemned plaza, Rosalind plays both tapes publicly and speaks the sentence they've carried since age nine — naming the enforcer, the cover-up, and their father. The room splits between fury and relief; Tomás stands beside them. POV Rosalind. Beat: climax — truth spoken at irreversible cost.

chapters.title: A Language, Remaining
chapters.summary: Months later, the case reopens and the enforcer is charged; the Old Quarter's archive, saved by the assembly, preserves Mateo's recordings. Rosalind translates the song's lyrics into the fading language and finds the lost words returning as they speak them aloud. POV Rosalind. Beat: resolution — memory kept, loyalty renegotiated, voice recovered.
